name: Libra
introduction: is the Scales, the only zodiac constellation named after an object rather than a living being. Its stars were once the claws of the Scorpion. About 2,000 years ago, the Sun stood here at the September equinox, when day and night are of equal length, which may be why the scales were placed here. It is best seen on northern spring and summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Libra’s brightest stars still bear their old names: [Zubenelgenubi](hip:72622), “the southern claw”, and [Zubeneschamali](hip:74785), “the northern claw”. Some observers report that Zubeneschamali has a greenish tint, which would make it unique among naked-eye stars, though the effect is likely an illusion.
In 2024, the Gaia mission revealed [Gaia NS1](id:gaia-ns1), a dormant neutron star in a wide orbit around a Sun-like star, betrayed only by its gravitational pull.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Zubenelgenubi](hip:72622) is a wide double star that sharp eyes can split. [Zubeneschamali](hip:74785) is a hot blue-white star 185 light-years away. [Brachium](hip:73714) is a red giant, and [Zubenelhakrabi](hip:76333) a yellow giant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Libra contains Gliese 581, a red dwarf with several planets, and the faint globular cluster NGC 5897.
